notes.title: Composite Bow Mechanics Rework | DevLog #23
notes.notes: [p]Hello Survivors, [/p][p][/p][p]We’re back to share our progress on the game, which is only possible because of your continued interest and support. Today, we're sharing news about the rework of the 'Composite Bow,' the exclusive weapon for the LOCKDOWN class.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h2][b]A Brief Introduction to the LOCKDOWN Class[/b][/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/46954e4701f395e3ad2ae8ea02c9dd6ed8e73b2b.jpg"][/img][/p][p]LOCKDOWN is a class that controls the battlefield by combining traps with ranged attacks. [/p][p]The core of its gameplay is to take the initiative in combat by luring or disabling enemies with traps, and then seizing control of the fight with ranged attacks from the bow.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Intention Behind the Rework[/b] [/h2][p]During the Tech Test last July, many of you left valuable feedback regarding the Composite Bow. In particular, many commented that [b]"the bow feels clunky to handle"[/b] and [b]"aiming and shooting feel awkward."[/b] Indeed, the process from aiming to firing was cumbersome, which often leaving players vulnerable. [/p][p]Therefore, our team decided to rework the mechanics of the Composite Bow to improve these aspects. This change is not just a tweak to the bow's performance, but also a process to more clearly define the identity of LOCKDOWN as the only class that can use a bow. [/p][p]Our goal was to get closer to LOCKDOWN's combat concept of [b]"herding enemies with traps and finishing them with the bow."[/b][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Major Changes to the Composite Bow[/b] [/h2][p]In this rework, we focused on improving the handling of the bow and enhancing the tempo of combat.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Overall Motion Changes[/b] [/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/a97b038635f9e00bbc5ce99e33797be54ce8ecba.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]The animation for drawing and shooting the bow has been overhauled.[/b] [/p][p]With the overall motion made smoother, you'll now see LOCKDOWN handle the bow much more naturally. We hope this leads to a more responsive combat experience.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Improved Attack Method[/b] [/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/c1ab6e3b2f35de358d19c7dec7595338f74bb740.gif"][/img][/p][p]Previously, the bow was aimed with a right-click and fired with a left-click. When aiming, the crosshair would disappear, making it difficult to tell where the arrow would go. [/p][p][b]This has now been changed so you can draw and fire the bow with just a left-click.[/b] [/p][p]The crosshair also remains visible, allowing for much clearer and more intuitive shooting.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Introduction of an Aiming Time Limit[/b] [/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/76c95246f2154b5a924005c39b24c06f3b827e4f.gif"][/img][/p][p]The ability to hold the bow drawn indefinitely has been changed [b]so that you can only hold the draw for a certain period.[/b] [/p][p]This removes the unrealistic situation of prolonged aiming and enhances the tension and tempo of combat.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Removal of Melee Attack[/b] [/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/e400d816e12c97f613c48335f533280b83b62293.gif"][/img][/p][p]We have [b]removed the melee attack[/b] where you would swing the bow with a left-click. [/p][p]The bow will now be established as a weapon focused exclusively on ranged combat.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]This Composite Bow rework was made possible thanks to the valuable feedback you gave us. Your opinions will continue to be a great source of strength as we refine the gameplay experience of our weapons and classes. [/p][p][/p][p]If you have more thoughts or ideas, please feel free to share them in the official [url="https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers"]The Midnight Walkers Discord community[/url]. Our team always welcomes feedback from our Survivors. We’ll keep working hard to raise the game’s quality to repay your support.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you.[/p]

notes.title: Dev Log#20
notes.notes:
[p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/f5f4870ac8ff310281f6a86f791ee3eb2df2d60b.png"][/img]As you know, a microphone is a tool meant to capture voices.
Some might have confessed their love through it,
others may have offered comfort,
and someone likely sang to a crowd with it.

But on the day this world collapsed under the zombie virus,
what was the last sound that mic captured?
Screams, distress calls, shattering glass.
And finally silence.

No longer able to record any sound,
someone still picked it up.
From that moment on, the mic spoke again.
Not with words or music, but with the cracking of skulls.

Once a vessel of voice,
the microphone is now a weapon of destruction.
Its memories are sealed with wire,
its silence shattered by impact.
All that’s left is a reason to make it ring once more.
[/p]

[h3][Design Intent: Structuring for Flow and Continuity][/h3]
[p]
The Junk Wrench may look like a hastily assembled weapon,
but our goal was to ensure it sustains the rhythm of combat without interruption.

Once you start swinging, the flow shouldn’t stop.
To create that flow, we focused on three core design principles:

We minimized delays between basic attacks,
so as long as you continue your input,
the motion keeps chaining naturally.

We also allowed players to branch out into strong attacks, dodges, or sub-weapon switches
without delay even with rapid input ensuring a smooth and responsive combat feel.

Though the weapon appears heavy,
the goal is for it to start with a weighty first hit,
and then gain speed through chained inputs,
offering a tactile rhythm that players can master over time.

This structure isn’t just about enabling combos
it’s about letting survivors feel like they are creating the momentum themselves.
[/p]

[h3][Form and Materials: Chaos with Purpose][/h3]
[p]
At first glance, the Junk Wrench might look like urban debris slapped together,
but its design is carefully calculated to achieve maximum impact with minimal resources.

● Mic Head: Visual focal point of strikes; gives the weapon identity
● Steel Pipe + Bolts: Focuses the weight forward to amplify impact
● Rusty Wire: Holds the structure and adds a damaged, chaotic aesthetic
● Sports Rubber Band: Prevents slipping and provides color contrast

This is not a crude assembly by a desperate survivor,
but a purpose-built structure, crafted by someone with technical intent.
And we hoped this asymmetrical design would give players
a visceral sense of what makes the Junk Wrench unique.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/4bf59ca9d3f177185c58c130174ee4cbf6ff4b25.jpg"][/img]
[/p]

[h3][Black Market Entry Route][/h3]
[p]
The Junk Wrench is not an officially sanctioned weapon.
But its internal structure, joining techniques, and parts layout
follow the exact blueprint standards of known manufacturers.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/c4322073f57e2cacacc9b8a5315f902b4b22b664.jpg"][/img]
So far, it seems the weapon is being circulated in limited numbers
via a black market route near the abandoned concert hall in southern Liberty Grand.
There are confirmed sightings of survivors actively using this weapon.

In the game world, it's still unclear
whether this weapon is an intentional design leak
or a unique modification crafted in the field.
But one thing is certain survivors may hesitate at first,
but they never want to let go once it’s in their hands.
[/p]

[h3][Behind the Design][/h3]
[p]
To finalize the Junk Wrench,
our team experimented with numerous scrap designs, starting from junk piles.
Pipe-based structures, giant wrench forms,
even weirdly mechanical combinations.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/c66e1f040894242ba5441c6110bcbd662b8bc344.jpg"][/img]
Some of them had us asking, “Who would even make this?”
Others looked too polished—like mass-produced factory tools.

In the end, our criteria were simple:
“It should look painful to get hit by,”
and
“It should feel like someone really scavenged urban remains to build it.”

That’s how we landed on this bizarre-but-believable combo
of mic head, pipe, wire, and rubber bands.

Too intimidating, and it stops feeling homemade.
Too clean, and it becomes forgettable.
We found that the right amount of strangeness was the most realistic.

Because that’s what junk is.
[/p]

[h3][In Closing][/h3]
[p]
What kind of weapon do you want to swing?
We're always open to your weapon ideas and feedback on Discord.
Our dev team wants to create weapons born from the combinations you imagine.
[url="https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers"] Join The Midnight Walkers Official Discord[/url]
[/p]

notes.title: Dev Log#19
notes.notes:
[h2]Junk Sledgehammer – The Weight That Demands Respect[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/2bbd03f2289d31a6920a941d81f6e88c08de5c36.png[/img]

The weapon we’re introducing this time is the [b]Junk Sledgehammer[/b].
At first glance, it may seem like nothing more than a chunk of iron,
but behind its crude form lies a great deal of careful thought.
With this weapon, we wanted to ask a question beyond raw strength
[b]“How do you handle this kind of weight?”[/b]

[h3]Answering the question: "Why did we make this?"[/h3]

Blunt weapons are notoriously difficult to handle in games.
They’re slow, heavy, and require precise timing.
But that’s exactly why we chose to make this hammer.
We wanted to create a weapon that could [b]turn the tide of battle with one strike[/b],
and a weapon where [b]the weight itself defines how you play[/b].

[h3]It’s heavy but not thrown together[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/04bdd34b9f0211fa6fa3ad0782520db3cf5707da.jpg[/img]

The head is based on steel structures used in actual railroads.
Both ends can be used for striking, and the forward-heavy balance delivers serious impact with each swing.

Instead of simple welding, we reinforced the core with bolts and nuts 
a functional solution we implemented after test builds revealed shaking and instability.

The handle is wrapped in duct tape, electrical tape, and a greasy rag.
These aren’t just for looks—they’re based on real survival tools for [b]grip and shock absorption[/b].

[h3]In-game role: A strike you can trust[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/ddfdb3537764d92b4cc32977c203028954f29eba.jpg[/img]

The Junk Sledgehammer is one of the heaviest two-handed weapons in the game.
It’s slow to swing, but [b]one hit can turn the tide[/b].
[b]Horizontal attacks[/b] push multiple enemies away and cause stagger—perfect for crowd control.
[b]Vertical strikes[/b] are effective against armored zombies and tanky enemies, dealing massive stagger or knockback, sometimes even fatal blows.

This weapon shines when:

Enemies rush you in tight interiors

You need silent but powerful impact

You're down to one last shot—[b]and it needs to count[/b]

[h3]Design Intent: Strategic weight players can feel[/h3]

The Junk Sledgehammer wasn’t created just to add another powerful weapon.
We wanted to give players the following experiences:

[b]1. A weapon that shifts combat rhythm[/b]
Unlike fast-striking weapons, this hammer [b]makes every hit a decision[/b].
You wait, read your opponent, and commit. We wanted every swing to feel like a moment.

[b]2. Control and spacing through impact[/b]
More than just damage, it’s a [b]tool to reset combat flow[/b] using knockback and stagger
letting players regain initiative and space.

[b]3. A last resort you can truly count on[/b]
Even when resources run out,
we wanted this weapon to offer the confidence that [b]you still have a way to survive[/b].
This isn't just a blunt object. It's a statement.

[h3]Comment[/h3]

The Junk Sledgehammer isn’t flashy,
but [b]it changes how you fight[/b].

It’s not easy to swing,
but landing the hit feels better than almost anything else.

If you’ve tried it out and have thoughts good or bad
come let us know on [url=https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers]Discord[/url].
Your feedback is the compass that guides us forward.

notes.title: Dev Log#18
notes.notes:
"That katana?  
In the black market, nameless weapons sometimes float around in silence.  
Among them...  
[b]Whoever made this one, they knew how to use a katana and they had taste."[/b]  
It was first discovered on the outskirts of a city left in ruins by the zombie virus,  
in a collapsed zone where surveillance and records no longer existed.  
After the outbreak, gunfire and explosions only attracted more infected,  
and the demand for quiet, decisive melee weapons soared.  
The Junk Katana was born to answer that need.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/6bfac206d4b994970c21b959ae3eaf70df83c486.png[/img]  
Forged from scraps of steel, worn pipes, and pieces of industrial gears.  
But the structure was too efficient to be a coincidence
the weight distribution, the wrapping on the grip, even the welds that bind blade and guard.  
It had to be a product born from the post-virus weapons market.

[h2]An Assembled Weapon[/h2]  
The Junk Katana isn’t just a chunk of scrap metal pieced together.  
Its blade is composed of different welded steel plates, marked by rust, dents, and scars of the past.  
Yet when you imagine swinging it, the weight balance reveals precise calculation.  
The guard appears crude, cut from a piece of industrial gear 
but its width and weight are just right for a guard’s purpose.  
It’s more than just defense. Perhaps it was designed  
to hold off sudden zombie charges in narrow hallways and enclosed spaces.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/1e0db29056de4e49e2afdf3e5c2c38f5ea56e3ee.jpg[/img]  
The grip follows a traditional tsuka style katana wrapping.  
Its texture rough yet rhythmic lets your fingers naturally fall into place.  
This isn’t decoration.  
It’s a structure born from the instincts of those who’ve actually swung it.

[h2]Design Philosophy[/h2]  
Our team never intended the Junk Katana to be “just another junk-tier weapon.”  
It was designed with the idea of what survivors might truly need  
in a world ravaged by the zombie virus.  
Tight corridors. Collapsing buildings. Overrun safehouses.  
In a world where a single gunshot could bring doom,  
survivors needed something silent… but deadly.  
The Junk Katana was imagined as a weapon built to be used
not in fantasy, but in those very real situations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/01a88ee8519fa2ed198772dd595b62914b152528.jpg[/img]  
From the reference sheet above, you can see:  
this weapon isn't pure fiction it’s built on real, tangible design logic.  
A guard inspired by turbine gears.  
A blade mimicking dismantled railway parts.  
A grip modeled after industrial piping.  
A handle wrapped in the tsuka style of Japanese katana.

Trace each reference, and questions naturally arise:  
Why this material? Why this weld? Why this balance?  
And that curiosity 
That is the immersion we wanted to build into the Junk Katana.

[h2]In Closing[/h2]  
The Junk Katana isn’t a finished weapon.  
No one knows who designed it or who assembled it.  
Its identity is shaped by your interpretation.

Design ideas, personal impressions, imagined backstories
we welcome all feedback and discussion on our [url=https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers]official Discord[/url].

As for the next public playtest many of you have been waiting for
we’re actively discussing it internally and will share news as soon as we can.  
Thank you as always for your patience and support.

notes.title: Bolt Action Rifle Design Rework
notes.notes:
Ruined cities, collapsed societies, and a world where only survival remains.
The weapons in The Midnight Walkers are gradually changing to reflect this grim reality.
In this devlog, we’d like to introduce the design rework of the bolt-action rifle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/eb413a5b2514791ba65474aacd37db3d312c3c60.png[/img]

[h2]Background of the Design Rework[/h2]

While the original bolt-action rifle had no issues in terms of performance, its clean and refined look felt slightly out of place in a post-apocalyptic world.
So, the goal of this rework was clear:
"Make it look like a weapon that belongs in this world."

Even after governments and military forces collapsed, some gunsmiths and engineers survived, dispersing into shelters, settlements, and underground arms networks.
They repaired and created weapons by request from survivor communities.
With traditional supply chains gone, they had to reuse existing materials and assemble weapons in different ways.

These weapons are often distributed unofficially through local arms dealers or the black market.
No formal structure, no standard design.
Yet, they are the only type of firepower survivors can trust in this world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/66dd8c351a88af8fdc113020cd08a817f51fa6c8.jpg[/img]

[h2]Same Performance, Enhanced Immersion[/h2]

This rework does not affect the weapon’s performance or balance in any way.
The bolt-action rifle retains its reload speed, range, and functionality.
Only the appearance and atmosphere have changed—to deepen visual immersion.

[previewyoutube=VEjSB7HFjU8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Key Design Elements[/h2]

[b]Stock Made from Water Pipes[/b]
A stock assembled from rusted pipes, bolts, and nuts. Crude, but resilient.
The sharp bolts suggest potential use in close combat—reflecting the creativity and desperation of its maker.

[b]Electrical Tape and Bandage Texture[/b]
Secured with electrical tape and wrapped in worn textures, this gives the impression of makeshift repairs, and adds a tactile sense when held.

[b]Recycled Wooden Parts[/b]
Instead of manufactured parts, the grip appears to be carved from salvaged furniture.
Its rough shape and stained surface show just how desperate its designer was.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/911a2f2652a32c623e1a40544d51b00b3a4709e1.png[/img]

[h2]How Is This Weapon Distributed?[/h2]

We envisioned this weapon not as a homemade gun, but as a product of a post-zombie weapon ecosystem.

There are small groups of engineers and gunsmiths who still operate, often connected to survivor communities or underground markets.
The bolt-action rifle is one such weapon—built on their workbenches.

A structure based on salvaged parts rather than standardized components.
A design philosophy that values simplicity for ease of repair and upkeep.
Unofficially distributed, and slightly different in detail with every unit—fully customized.

This setup not only explains the weapon’s look but also strengthens the worldbuilding.
It’s the kind of weapon that makes survivors wonder:
"Where did that come from?"

[h2]Future Plans and Feedback[/h2]

This design rework is more than just a visual update.
We aim to better express the core theme of The Midnight Walkers: "The reality of those who survive the end."
Other weapons will also be reworked in this direction.

How did you feel about the rework of the bolt-action rifle?
Join our [url=https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers]official Discord[/url] and share your thoughts.
Your feedback helps us build a more immersive world.

notes.title: Dev Log#16
notes.notes:
The infected in The Midnight Walkers are not just mindless zombies.
We never wanted to create enemies that simply inspire fear.
Instead, we wanted each one to carry traces of who they were before they turned.
So that when survivors face them, they can feel—"What kind of life did this person live? And how did it all fall apart?"

In this devlog, we’d like to introduce our latest zombie designs and the stories woven into them.
Why do they look like this? What moment marked their turning point?

[h2]1. Who Never Left the Hospital[/h2]

The concept for the doctor walker began with a simple but chilling idea:
“A doctor who continues to see patients, unaware of his own death.”
A stethoscope still around his neck, a headlamp on his forehead, and a blood-soaked coat.
Their hands still search for patients or perhaps, prey.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/cfc94845c104368cca0c3f68f2c3ca04dd6ed2ae.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/5555535dc4fe4ca1478c467adecd5472f2552449.png[/img]

They never left the hospital.
Even as the medical system collapsed, he remained by their patients’ sides, risking his life to save others.
But in the end, they became one of the first to be infected.

The hands once stretched out for healing are now a deadly threat.
Their white coat is no longer a symbol of care,
but a tragic remnant of how quickly this world crumbled.

[h2]2. A Tragedy in the Heart of the City[/h2]

The woman walker was designed to feel like the most “urban” infected.
Barefoot after kicking off her high heels, dressed as if she was headed for a date, her hair slightly undone.
We didn’t want her to be overtly terrifying.
Instead, we wanted players to feel a realistic, immersive kind of horror.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/1ddaadb445cac4da36397530826b795251fac00d.png[/img]

She was just an ordinary office worker.
It was a Friday evening, and she had plans—finally.
Her last message read: "Almost at the subway~ :)"

But that night, the subway she arrived at wasn’t a normal one.
It had already fallen—overrun by the infected.

Even now, she wanders the city in that same outfit,
still trapped in that night,
as if searching for the person she was supposed to meet, following the footsteps of survivors.

[h2]3. The One Remembered by Her Scream[/h2]

This zombie was designed not as a direct threat,
but as a screeching siren that draws in nearby walkers with her voice.
The focal point of her design is her mouth.
A torn jaw, swollen neck, and grotesquely widened maw—all meant to visually express the brutal violence of her sound.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/3c5d9ebccd5f04c603c2804cdc4db0fa3372683d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/4637e31b9912da04fb9b1ca450effbdf41e8cd32.png[/img]

But what we really wanted to portray wasn't just the sound—it was the story buried beneath her scream.

Was she once a performer, singing on stage?
Or a patient in a hospital room, screaming in pain?
She still seems to be crying out to someone, endlessly.
It might be a call for help, a scream of grief, or simply an echo of memory.

No one knows for sure.
But her voice has become despair incarnate.

[h2]4. The Steps That Never Stopped[/h2]

When we first explored the concept of a “runner zombie,” we didn’t want it to just be fast.
We wanted it to have a reason to run.

So we thought of someone who would sprint into danger rather than away from it—
someone who would risk everything to save others.
A firefighter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/9c916df18d37dfba4585180a8c9429ce47303369.png[/img]

He was once a hero who rushed into flames and crumbling buildings to rescue those trapped inside.
Now, he runs just as fast—but toward survivors, to hunt them down.
His heavy fireproof gear still clings to his body,
but the flesh within is already twisted and warped, infected at a terrifying pace.

And yet he still runs.
The silhouette of a rescuer has become a monstrous blur of death.
The instinct that once drove him toward saving lives,
now fuels a relentless sprint toward ending them.

[h2]5. A Tragedy Without End[/h2]

We will continue to show how people from all walks of life were dragged into the same despair.
Each resident of Liberty Grand Center had their own hopes, duties, and relationships—
but when the infection came, those lives were torn apart without warning.

Some were infected while waiting to be rescued.
Some got lost while trying to flee.
Some were turned while protecting someone else.

They are no longer human.
But within their twisted forms are fragments of who they once were.
What we’re creating isn’t just a roster of enemies.
It’s the unspoken history of Liberty Grand City.
And soon, you’ll come face to face with that history yourself.

[h2]6. In Closing[/h2]

We plan to continue expanding the world of The Midnight Walkers
through unique designs and stories that carry the weight of this world’s fall.

Your fears, your sadness, your imagined stories—
they all help us shape this world into something richer and more haunting.

Join us on Discord and share your thoughts.
Tell us what kinds of walkers you’d like to see, what stories you want us to tell.
Let’s build it together!

notes.title: Dev Log#15
notes.notes:
If you thought it was just another dangerous zombie, this devlog will reveal the Spitter's true power.
More than just a toxic liquid spewing entity, the Spitter is designed to challenge your strategic thinking and cooperation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/3d44098982ad894c2a42b406efc05b0922687178.png[/img]

[h2]1. The Spitter’s Background[/h2]
The Liberty Grand Center may have seemed like a mere refuge to survivors, but in truth, it was nothing less than Mr. Nobody’s experimental lab.
For those who sought hope, it became a place of despair, pain, and horrific experiments.

The Spitter is the result of experiments conducted on individuals who sought refuge but were physically weaker or injured.
After successfully transforming stronger individuals into the melee-focused Charger zombie, Mr. Nobody and his organization began focusing their experiments on long-range toxic capabilities, resulting in the creation of the Spitter.

Unlike the Charger, who embodies physical dominance, the Spitter is a product of the same experiments designed to maximize viral diversity, targeting even the weaker survivors.
This divergence has led the Spitter to evolve into a completely different kind of threat.
Its ability to generate toxic substances has made it a subject of fear among survivors.

The Spitter was no accident—it was purposefully designed by Mr. Nobody as a toxic-focused “experimental subject.”
According to records left in the Liberty Grand Center, this toxic substance wasn’t just meant to harm survivors but was also used to study the virus’s potential for environmental spread.

[h2]2. Combat Tips for Facing the Spitter[/h2]
Fighting the Spitter requires a completely different approach compared to other zombies. It presents a unique and nerve-wracking challenge.

[previewyoutube=MVI5tppNeSI;full][/previewyoutube]
※ The video was recorded in a test environment and may show some stuttering.
Please note that the actual gameplay environment is expected to run smoothly.
● Long-Range Attacks: The Spitter applies constant pressure by spewing toxic liquid from a distance. Avoid its range whenever possible.
● Health Management: If you’re hit by its toxic attack, you’ll suffer from a poisoning effect, taking continuous damage. Bring healing items and try to avoid direct contact.
● Final Explosion: Upon death, the Spitter unleashes a toxic explosion. If you’re within the blast radius, you’ll take significant damage. Maintain a safe distance as it nears death.

[h2]3. Are You Ready to Face the Spitter?[/h2]
The Spitter brings new terror and excitement to the world of The Midnight Walkers.
Facing it will test your strategy and teamwork like never before.

Experience the Spitter in action during the upcoming final public test this February!
Got thoughts about the Spitter? Share them with us in our [url=https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers]Discord community[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/d5161304c4be1cea5a8406f1d0922b181fab2b4f.png[/img]
The Charger is a mid boss tier zombie with an intense presence.
Each of its attacks is a serious threat, and without teamwork among squads, it is nearly impossible to take it down.
From its appearance to its abilities, everything about the Charger is designed to make your heart race.

[h2]1. The Charger’s Background[/h2]

As the virus caused the world to collapse, people sought refuge in what they believed to be a safe haven, Liberty Grand Center, located in Gold County.
But sadly, this was no ordinary refuge.
This location was controlled by "Mr. Nobody" and his organization, who seemed to be protecting survivors but were secretly conducting experiments behind the scenes.

Among those who sought safety at the refuge, individuals who enjoyed sports, were physically fit, or had strong physiques like rugby players became prime candidates for experiments.
For survivors with families, they were given the harsh choice: “Your life or your family’s?” On the other hand, for those without families, weaker individuals or even children were used as leverage, subjecting them to torture and threats to force participation in the experiments.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/bd7727943df065ecef221c8e9787fe0dc488df59.png[/img]
Mr. Nobody’s goal was not only to create powerful zombies but also to study the various reactions of the virus through specific zombie transformations.
The results of these experiments produced creatures with entirely different traits and abilities compared to standard walkers.
Of these, the Charger was one of the most dangerous and powerful outcomes.

[h2]2. Charger’s Skills and Abilities[/h2]

The Charger possesses extraordinary abilities that exceed your expectations. Its charge skill is not only a threat but also a game-changer in battles. Its devastating attacks bring both tension and excitement.

● Key Features
- Close-range attacks
- Charging ability
- Charge combo
- Damage: Instant damage and knockback effect
- Health: Significantly higher than standard zombies
- Speed: Moderate movement speed; rapid acceleration during charges

Watch the test version video below for more details.
[previewyoutube=qVUGUxtWx3c;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]※ This footage was captured in the test version and may differ from the final release. ※[/b]
When it charges, survivors are highly advised to evade its path.

[h2]3. How to Deal with the Charger[/h2]

Battling the Charger without cooperation or experience can be extremely challenging.
Understanding its patterns and devising effective strategies will be key to success.
Prepare strong equipment and skills.
Most importantly, learning when to back off is the ultimate key to dealing the Charger.

[h2]4. Prepare to Face the Charger[/h2]

The Charger is here to make your heart pound and ignite your desire for a challenge.
Its overwhelming presence is not just that of an enemy—it’s a monumental challenge you must overcome, and that is our goal.
If you have any thoughts about the Charger, please feel free to leave your feedback on our [url=https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers]Discord[/url].

notes.title: Dev Log #13
notes.notes:
[h2]A Dynamic Experience: Floor Rotation System[/h2]
Survivors, Liberty Grand Center is evolving beyond a mere survival ground. It’s becoming a strategic battleground where tension and strategy collide. In this development diary, we’re excited to introduce our ongoing work on the Floor Rotation System, designed to deliver a thrilling and constantly changing survival experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/ae2f7ca240de513de39fef36061d961e6e941ed4.png[/img]

[h2]1. Overview of the Floor Rotation System[/h2]
The Floor Rotation System aims to achieve the following goals, while Liberty Grand Center will eventually expand to over 24 floors with more themed battle zones in development:

Offer new exploration opportunities with diverse floors to enhance gameplay experiences.
Create unpredictable scenarios to amplify tension and immersion.
Design ever-changing routes to make each session feel fresh and engaging.
This system will rotate the available floors at fixed intervals, encouraging survivors to embrace new challenges with each rotation.

[h2]2. Core Design Features[/h2]
Survivors can preview the current active floors and the upcoming rotation in advance, with battle grounds remaining fixed for a set duration.

● Rotation Timer
At the end of each interval, the active floor range will automatically shift to new levels. Survivors will see a real-time countdown to the next rotation.
For example, matches may initially occur on lower floors (B1-7F) for 10 minutes, before shifting to upper floors (8F-16F), offering new routes and strategies.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/c049f39c213c432981c7c282037dff0a0f18034f.png[/img]
Our ultimate goal is to ensure seamless and uninterrupted gameplay by minimizing split matchmaking pools.

● Global Synchronization
To maintain a fair gaming environment, the active floor ranges will be synchronized globally for all survivors. This design prevents fragmented matchmaking and ensures everyone shares the same experience.

[h2]3. Enhanced UI and User Experience[/h2]
The Floor Rotation System will be accompanied by an intuitive UI, ensuring a smooth experience for survivors. Separate floor ranges will be designated for solo and team modes. Below is a preview of the updated UI.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/ce91d5bbbaf82c2a7b8ab0a9d5d4f7de75da4a41.png[/img]
[b]Please note: The UI shown is still under development and not final.[/b]

●  Current and Upcoming Floor Information
For example, the team mode may currently be active on floors B1-7F, with the next rotation scheduled for floors 8F-15F. Survivors can plan their strategies using clear, real-time information on when the rotation will occur.

[h2]4. Changes the System Will Bring[/h2]
As mentioned, Liberty Grand Center will see the addition of more themed floors over time. The rotation system’s ultimate goal is to deliver fresh and exciting experiences every time survivors enter the game.

Elevators and staircases will play a critical role. Some floors may restrict access to these features, forcing survivors to rethink their strategies. Furthermore, we’re exploring the possibility of random events occurring in certain areas to inject moments of unpredictable tension.

[h2]5. Future Plans[/h2]
The Floor Rotation System is currently in its early stages of design and testing. As always, your feedback is invaluable to us in refining and enhancing this feature.

Your thoughts and ideas inspire us every day. Please feel free to share your feedback and suggestions on our [url=https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers]Discord channel[/url].
Stay tuned for more updates, and thank you for your continued support.

notes.title: Dev Log#11

[h2]1. Single Barrel Shotgun[/h2]

Our development team envisioned what it would feel like for survivors to hold this weapon in the post-apocalyptic world of The Midnight Walkers. We aimed to create more than just a gun — we wanted to portray the "will to survive" that emerges in a desolate world.

In the previous test, survivors had access to the Double Barrel Shotgun. While its powerful firepower captured players' attention, it also presented an unexpected overbalance issue. As a result, other weapons were overshadowed, pushing our team to rethink the situation.

Ultimately, the team decided not to abandon the shotgun entirely but to refine it. By transitioning to the Single Barrel Shotgun, we aimed to retain the shotgun's strengths while encouraging survivors to make more deliberate and strategic decisions.

[h2]2. Modeling Changes[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/ed292b5827691cd2ba398fc04802be99bae10292.png[/img]  
Here is the updated model of the Single Barrel Shotgun. To preserve the original atmosphere, we incorporated rusty metal pipes, worn leather, and aged tape to reflect the hardships and struggles of survival.

[h2]3. Performance Changes[/h2]

The Single Barrel Shotgun fires only one round at a time, but that single shot represents a survivor's decisive judgment. Every shot carries weight, making each decision meaningful.  
With the shift to a single shot, the reload speed has slightly improved compared to the Double Barrel Shotgun. However, the tension of carefully managing each round will make the experience even more intense than before.

[h2]4. Conclusion[/h2]

We are currently conducting extensive internal tests to refine and improve the game. This effort extends not only to the Single Barrel Shotgun but also to newly added floors and zombies, all of which are undergoing rigorous evaluation and adjustment.

Our goal is to bring you closer to the day when you can wield this weapon and enjoy combat in Liberty Grand Center.  
We sincerely appreciate the patience and support of all survivors, and we remain committed to delivering an even more polished gaming experience.  

We’ll return soon with more exciting news.  
Thank you.

notes.title: Dev Log#10
notes.notes:
[h2]The Origin of the Scrap Spear[/h2]

A weapon forged at the edge of survival—the Scrap Spear is truly the epitome of survival instincts.  
Metal fragments discovered in the ruins of Liberty Grand Center, old ropes, and rusted pipes were transformed into a single weapon by human hands.  
This spear is not just a tool to attack enemies but a symbol of the survivor’s wisdom and adaptability to harsh environments.

In the early stages of development, our team started with the concept of "a weapon crafted from scrap or junk materials."  
Below are the various design concepts of the Scrap Spear created during the initial planning phase.  
Each design reflects how the Scrap Spear could take form and survive in the game world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/277f4a65933cbef46c736355e3f87825b9a4764a.png[/img]
Let’s take a closer look at each design’s characteristics:

- Design 1: A traditional spear blended with the resourcefulness of a survivor.  
- Design 2: A design that emphasizes industrial aesthetics and rugged practicality.  
- Design 3: A destructive design that incorporates a saw blade to maximize danger.  
- Design 4: A simple yet lethal design optimized for practical use.  
- Design 5: The final chosen design, achieving perfect balance with its use of diverse materials.  

Our development team ultimately chose Design 5.  
This design best captures the essence of a "rough but reliable" survival weapon.

[h2]The Final Concept of the Scrap Spear[/h2]

The final design of the Scrap Spear can be described as a raw masterpiece, brought to life through the hands of a survivor.  
Its sharp blade, made from rusted metal fragments, its pole crafted from old pipes, and its bindings secured with rope emphasize the spear’s unique personality.  
Below is the finalized concept art of the Scrap Spear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/8040d1b49eac9c27f6f18f91cc6c54f4758ba82f.png[/img]
*The name has not been finalized.*

This Scrap Spear is versatile, capable of both thrusting and slashing attacks to adapt to various combat situations.  
Its long reach allows survivors to strike from a safe distance, enriching combat strategies.

[h2]Modeling[/h2]

After finalizing the concept art, a high-resolution model was created to bring it to life.  
Below is the final model image, which faithfully recreates every detail of the concept art.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/16cf004d2fb3bc9b4dea6987d425f963603dda91.png[/img]

The modeling process focused on the following key aspects:
- The rough texture of rusted metal: Enhances realism and immersion while emphasizing its role as a survival tool.  
- Harmonization of scrap materials: Includes bolts, pipes, and ropes that could be found in survival environments.  
- Tactile combat design: Ensures players feel the tension and ruggedness of survival when wielding the spear.

[h2]Attack Patterns[/h2]

The Scrap Spear isn’t just about its long reach.  
It provides diverse attack patterns, allowing survivors to tailor their combat style to suit various situations.  
Here are the basic attack patterns of the Scrap Spear:

- Thrust (1st Hit): A sharp forward thrust aimed at the crosshair.  
- Slash (2nd Hit): A powerful slash directed in a specific direction.  
- Thrust (3rd Hit): A forward strike delivered with a powerful upward thrust.

[h2]Future Plans[/h2]

The Scrap Spear is currently in the testing phase and will soon be available for survivors to experience in a future update.  
Based on your feedback and ideas, we plan to further refine and improve this weapon.  
If you have any thoughts or suggestions after reading this dev diary, please visit our Discord to share your ideas. We’d love to hear from you.  
Thank you for your support!

notes.title: Upcoming Major Updates #1
notes.notes:
Hello, Survivors.  

This is Ray, the director of The Midnight Walkers.  

It has already been a month since the public alpha test began. Time really flies.  
During this time, the development team has reviewed your valuable feedback and survey responses and has been working hard to establish a more solid direction for development.  

Today, I’d like to share some confirmed features for the next test, which were finalized after discussions within the development team.  

Although the exact schedule for the next test has not yet been determined, we aim to share it with you soon. Additionally, we confirm our participation in the [b]Steam Next Fest[/b] in February next year.  

[h2]Parrying and Combat Improvements[/h2]
Yes, a parry system is being implemented. The development team agreed that additional actions were necessary to provide a deeper and more detailed combat experience, and therefore decided to implement the parry system.  

Currently, the parry system is under development, and we expect it to pair well with TMW’s charging attack system.  
We are also revising attack animations to create more tension-filled animations and are diversifying weapon trajectories. Additional combos are also under consideration.  

In summary, the implementation of the parry system will offer a more rhythmic and immersive experience in attack and defense gameplay.  
The charging attack system will complement this by creating richer combat patterns.  

As soon as the prototype is ready, we will share it on [url=https://discord.gg/themidnightwalkers]Discord[/url].  

[h2]Floor Rotation System[/h2]
In the previous test, you could experience floors from B1F to 7F. Now, you will be able to explore from B1F to 15F.  

Of course, experiencing all 16 floors in a single game would be time-consuming and make it harder to encounter other players.  
To address this, we have devised a floor rotation system where the accessible range changes every 10 minutes.  

The floors will be divided into three ranges:  
- B1F to 7F  
- 4F to 11F  
- 8F to 15F  

This system is being implemented for diversity and is subject to change based on your feedback during playtests.  
Enjoy the expanded Liberty Grand Center environment!  

[h2]Enhanced Crafting System and Grinder[/h2]
To diversify materials and craftable items, we are preparing a new menu called the Workshop.  

Instead of crafting items through merchants, you can now directly access the Workshop menu from the lobby to view all craftable items at a glance.  
This will provide a more convenient crafting experience.  

Additionally, grinders will be scattered throughout Liberty Grand Center.  
Survivors can use these machines to grind items and obtain lower-tier materials.  
Of course, this is only if you successfully extract!  

If you’ve played Rust, this system may feel familiar.  

[h2]Zombie AI Improvements and New Zombie Types[/h2]
We’re improving zombie AI and refining their attack animations.  
Our goal is to make attack motions clearer and give each zombie distinct characteristics.  

The existing zombie group (Walkers, Runners, and Tankers) will be joined by Spitters and Crawlers,  
adding variety and richness to long-range and close-range combat.  
Additionally, a new elite zombie, the Charger, will be introduced.  

Chargers are massive zombies that charge into and disrupt the players’ formations. Stay tuned!  

[h2]New Weapon and Weapon Rebalancing[/h2]
A new two-handed weapon, the Trash Spear, will be added. This melee weapon offers relatively long range, allowing for combat from a safer distance.  

Meanwhile, the Double Barrel Shotgun is being modified to a Single Barrel Shotgun.  
This change is due to the structural advantages the Double Barrel Shotgun had over other firearms, which required adjustments for balance.  

These are some of the confirmed updates the development team has been discussing recently.  
We’ll continue to transparently share updates as we outline our roadmap and vision.  

Thank you for your patience and support as we continue to develop this game.  

Sincerely,  
Director Ray

notes.title: Dev Log#8
notes.notes:
[h2]1. Background of the Spitter's Creation: The Fall of the Hotelier[/h2]
The Spitter was once an ordinary hotelier, but after the wave of infection swept through, it transformed into a horrifying creature that no one would want to approach. His former appearance is nowhere to be seen, twisted into something monstrous, yet he still “welcomes” guests in his own disturbing way. His deadly toxic spit from a distance is his new form of “greeting.” Every step the Spitter takes fills the area with a cold tension, and anyone who sees him up close can't help but step back instinctively.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/a4a7d918ec27dbe3fe00fb5e2afe4c5036234e1b.png[/img]

[h2]2. Abilities and Combat Style of the Spitter: A Distant Threat[/h2]
The Spitter is unlike typical zombies. From afar, it releases deadly toxins that threaten survivors. Getting hit by its spit doesn’t just hurt once; it inflicts continuous damage over time, slowly draining health. In confined spaces, its toxic attacks are even harder to avoid, adding an intense layer of suspense to any encounter with the Spitter.

The Spitter usually roams slowly around, but the moment it senses noise or movement, it heads in that direction immediately. The weighty steps and unsettling movements it takes during its search instill a chilling sense of fear in players. If you want to avoid a confrontation, staying out of its sight is your best option.

Once you’re in the Spitter's line of sight and battle begins, remember to keep your distance and dodge quickly. There’s a chance to avoid its toxic attacks, but missing that chance means you’ll have to bear the consequences. When you see the Spitter slowly approaching from afar, things have already gotten dangerous.

[h2]3. Finalizing the Spitter Concept[/h2]
The Spitter was initially conceived in various forms. Each concept aimed to heighten the horror aspect of the Spitter in different ways. Here are the initial concept ideas for the Spitter:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/19a04325053424efb7c2e6529f1c2c27199ceaf3.jpg[/img]

[h3]3-1. Hotelier Spitter[/h3]
The Hotelier Spitter, with bloodstained clothing and a toxic sac around its neck, was designed to spit poisonous substances from its mouth. The contrast between the pristine suit and the grotesque toxic sac added a creepy sense of horror. The hotelier background brought a peculiar vibe, merging formality with terror.

[h3]3-2. Elderly Woman Spitter[/h3]
This concept involved an elderly woman with a weak physique, retaining her frail appearance even after infection. However, her bloated stomach, filled with toxic substances, conveyed a sense of horror born from social vulnerability.

[h3]3-3. Pizza Delivery Spitter[/h3]
Once a busy pizza delivery person, this Spitter transformed with a grotesquely bloated stomach full of deadly toxins. Instead of a warm pizza, it now carries death. The contrast between its past and current state was intended to deliver a stronger visual impact.

[h3]3-4. Restrained Spitter[/h3]
The Restrained Spitter had its arms bound, unable to use them but still spitting poison as a form of attack. The sense of danger it conveyed, despite its restraints, was meant to heighten unease through its design (reflecting the concept artist’s personal preference).

Out of these varied ideas, the Hotelier Spitter was selected as the final concept. The formal yet horrifying appearance perfectly matched the Liberty Grand Center environment, conveying the Spitter’s horror in the most effective way.

Once modeling and animations are ready to showcase, we’ll share updates immediately. Please note that the Spitter is still in development and not yet finalized.
Thank you.

notes.title: Announcement of the next dev milestone
notes.notes:
Hello Survivors,
This is Ray, the director of The Midnight Walkers.
We began development in early August last year, conducted our first closed alpha test in May of this year, and recently ran our first public alpha test.

We received far more applicants for testing than expected—over ten times our initial estimate of 2,000. I want to take this opportunity to thank each of you for your incredible interest in The Midnight Walkers.

The alpha test was certainly full of ups and downs. Given the short development period and our desire to showcase as much as possible, there were several areas that fell short and unforeseen issues that impacted some players, resulting in the loss of precious time and items.

Despite these challenges, your patience and willingness to enjoy the game were invaluable, and we deeply appreciate it.

As we mentioned, we aim not to rely on "early access" as a shield but instead to improve and strengthen as many aspects of the game as possible from the start.

The unsatisfactory experiences from this test will be transformed into special and enjoyable gameplay that truly rewards you.

Our focus in this test was to verify and monitor the technical aspects and gameplay routines.

[i]The key focuses for our next development milestone are as follows:[/i]

[h2]1. Enhancing Core Fun and Unique Features of The Midnight Walkers[/h2]
Currently, Liberty Grand Center is composed of 8 floors, but we plan to expand it to over 20 floors. The development team has already built up to the 14th floor, and we are considering options for matchmaking through floor rotation or defining floor ranges while maintaining the current 8-floor rotation.

With the increase in floors, players can expect to experience various themes such as fitness clubs, spas, and casinos, allowing for more diverse gameplay environments. We are focused on crafting detailed gameplay experiences on each floor.

We also plan to improve the overall combat experience. Initially, due to rapid development, we missed several opportunities to revamp the combat system. Now, we aim to enhance the thrill of combat by redesigning attack motions and solidifying the unique characteristics of each weapon, providing more engaging offense and defense interactions.

Of course, zombies will play a central role in these improvements. We are upgrading AI patterns to create more satisfying combat encounters with zombies, and new zombie types will be introduced. These include zombies that spit tumor-like projectiles from a distance and others that target players' lower bodies by moving without their lower halves.

Based on our monitoring from this test, we will also improve UX to provide a more convenient experience, while focusing on a UI design that highlights the unique characteristics of The Midnight Walkers.

[h2]2. Balance[/h2]
While class distinctions are important, creating realistic combat situations is our priority, and we will now pay closer attention to fine-tuning each class. Active skills and perks will continue to be added to each class, with new abilities that will solidify each class’s unique traits.

We are moving from a phase focused on feature development to one centered on gameplay, so for the next test, we plan to conduct extensive PVE and PVP testing within the development team to create even more enjoyable combat experiences.

[h2]3. Reinforcing the Game Cycle[/h2]
The next test will be longer than a week, so we will work on enhancing the gameplay life cycle to ensure lasting enjoyment throughout the testing period.

This process will involve improvements to the crafting system, and, if resources permit, the introduction of a mission (Quest) system.

[h2]4. Technical Improvements and User-Friendly UX[/h2]
For the next test, we plan to implement a more precise anti-cheat system, build upon data gathered from this test, and make structural adjustments to provide a more stable server environment.

While it was challenging to test alongside everyone over the five-day period, the development team and I had a great time. We felt a range of emotions throughout the process.

Our team will now take time to reorganize and focus on development for the next test. We will continue to share the development process and communicate openly, as we have until now.

Thank you again to all testers who participated in the first alpha test of The Midnight Walkers!

Sincerely,
Director Ray and the One-Way Ticket Studio Development Team

notes.title: Devlog#7
notes.notes:
Hello, Survivors.
We would like to introduce the new class, the 'Bartender', who shakes a cocktail shaker even in the midst of Liberty Grand Center, full of zombies and enemies!
This character is not just a simple supporter. The Bartender can craft various drinks to empower their teammates, and at times, ignite their own blood to deliver powerful attacks on enemies as a versatile close-range warrior.
Look forward to seeing how the "Bartender who refreshes everyone's throats and heats up their hearts" will change your battles!
[b]The Bartender class is not final and may have its specs changed in future updates.[/b]

[h2][Character Concept and Design][/h2]
The Bartender is a character known as the "Cheerful Drinker." As the name suggests, they maintain a carefree attitude even in bleak environments. [b]Their specialty is drinking their own crafted drinks to unleash immense power or using those drinks to aid teammates.[/b] You will never see a Bartender grim-faced in battle! They always ask with a smile, "What would you like to drink today?"

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/68d3f8d7510c0b27ce469db051aa9baf63d96fbc.png[/img]

[h2][Unique Skill (Drink Crafting) System][/h2]
The Bartender's unique skill is their special drink crafting system. Like a chef, they can combine ingredients to craft special drinks. They can [b]power up teammates with an ‘Attack Boost Drink’,[/b] make them [b]invincible with a ‘Defense Boost Drink’,[/b] or sometimes toss a [b]‘Poison Drink’ to debilitate enemies.[/b] The fun lies in crafting the right drink for the situation and using it just like shaking a cocktail shaker.
To craft a drink, input the recipe by pressing the [←], [↑], [→], [↓] keys in the correct order. Once the drink is complete, press [F] to drink it yourself, or allow others to interact with it by pressing [F], or throw it at a target with a right-click.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/67e317060ce33897c8ea5b959a893c02c59edb54.png[/img]

[h3]① Ingredient Storage[/h3]
The first step in crafting drinks is the ingredient storage. Here, the Bartender can store and manage various ingredients used for crafting.

[b]● Ingredient List:[/b]
Bearberries, garlic, and chives are distinguished by their unique colors and icons, each providing different effects. For example, bearberries are used for healing recipes, while garlic is for strengthening.

[b]● Ingredient Capacity and Recovery Rate:[/b]
The storage capacity (e.g., 24/25) shows the current available ingredients, and only 25 total ingredients can be carried into the game.

[b]● Ingredient Replenishment:[/b]
Ingredients can be replenished through interaction in the field, and even if a player fails an extraction, basic ingredients will still be provided.

This system forms the foundation of the Bartender's drink crafting, and players must manage their ingredients efficiently to execute their unique recipes.

[h3]② Drink Crafting Recipes[/h3]
The second step is the drink crafting recipes. The Bartender can create special drinks through various combinations, which can be consumed by the Bartender or provided to others.

[b]● Recipe Tree:[/b] The recipe tree connects various drinks, allowing players to craft desired drinks by arranging ingredients. Each recipe has specific effects, and can be enhanced based on the character's traits.

[b]● Recipe Combinations:[/b] Drink effects vary based on the combinations, and skilled Bartenders can craft drinks that suit the team's situation.

[b]● Recipe Management:[/b] Slot 2 stores the in-game recipes. These cannot be changed in-game and must be set in the out-game interface before entering the battlefield. Players must prepare recipes tailored to the battlefield before the match begins.

[b]● Crafting Process:[/b] Drink crafting requires casting time, during which the Bartender mixes ingredients to complete the drink.
This system is crucial to the Bartender's battle strategy, with the effectiveness of the drinks highly dependent on the combinations used.

[h3]③ Skill List[/h3]
The final stage is the skill list. The Bartender can use crafted drinks to activate various skills, allowing them to dominate the battlefield.

[b]● Skill List and Effects:[/b]
The skill list features skills of varying grades, each requiring specific ingredient combinations for different effects. For example, the "Heart of Steel" skill provides high defense and resistance.

[b]● Ingredient Requirements:[/b]
Each skill requires specific combinations of ingredients, and higher-grade skills require more complex combinations.

[b]● Skill Management:[/b]
The skill list in Slot 3 is also managed in the out-game interface. Players can set which recipes to bring into the battle beforehand, ensuring they are prepared for various situations on the battlefield.

[h2][Active Skills][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/d2815875f5a0a1cd534c0cfb5a2fb64ed56609b0.png[/img]

[b]① Party Time:[/b]
"Shout in joy to increase movement speed by 15% and casting speed by 30% for 15 seconds."
This skill allows the Bartender to control the battlefield atmosphere and give the team an advantage. Use it before battle to boost team speed and attack.

[b]② Sweet Champagne:[/b]
Spray from a champagne bottle set on the ground to restore 5 HP per second to allies within 1.5m for 7 seconds.
This skill helps restore teammates’ HP in intense battles, turning the tide in your favor.

[b]③ Drink Enchant:[/b]
Coat a weapon with a toxic drink or smash a bottle to deal fixed damage and apply a poison debuff to nearby enemies.
This skill goes beyond just an attack, adding a poison debuff that drains enemy health over time.

[b]④ Drink Crafting:[/b]
Mix various ingredients to create a drink with specific effects. Drinks can be consumed or thrown, and their effects depend on the ingredients and order used. Players can maximize the drink's performance through special recipes.

[h2][Future Plans][/h2]
The Bartender you can experience in this public playtest is not the final version.
We plan to refine the drink crafting system to be more fun and creative, allowing for more varied combinations based on the situation. We will also add special events or animations during the crafting process to enhance this character’s unique playstyle. Based on your feedback, we will continue developing the Bartender to become the heart of team play.

"Take a moment to relax, even on the battlefield!" Meet the Bartender in the upcoming public playtest.

notes.title: Devlog#6
notes.notes:
Survivors, are you ready to uncover the hidden secrets of Liberty Grand Center?
In this dev log, we’re excited to introduce a new Lock and Unlock System that will provide you with a more strategic and immersive experience.

You’re about to face challenges beyond just defeating enemies. Now, you have the chance to find special keys or keycards to unlock doors and safes hidden throughout Liberty Grand Center, leading to exciting rewards.
Should you open every door you come across? Well, the treasure behind them may be tremendous, or you might encounter a powerful threat, no one knows for sure!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/04f291dafa07b11c439a04243dcc64139bb0c01e.png[/img]
[b]※Who knows? There might be something hidden behind the Tomato Statue※[/b]

[h2][Key Elements of the Unlock System][/h2]
The unlock system is designed to take your gameplay to the next level, adding depth to the game beyond just combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/3b71d114c84ab2c65a99b4025444eb5ff0336fcf.png[/img]

The types of safes will become more varied over time.
The designs are not final and may be subject to change.
[h3]●A New Experience of Finding Hidden Treasures:[/h3]
Instead of simply finding items, you’ll now be able to use special keys and keycards to unlock doors and safes and discover the treasures hidden inside.
Where you choose to use the key will be a significant decision.
Perhaps you’ll unlock the door to a [b]secret lab[/b], only to find yourself facing a powerful zombie.

[h3]●The Importance of Choice:[/h3]
Remember, a single choice can change your fate.
While you may find some of the best treasures hidden in Liberty Grand Center, terrifying enemies might be lurking as well.
No one can guarantee that opening a locked area is the right decision.

[h2][Development Details][/h2]

[h3]● How to Use Items:[/h3]
Once you obtain an unlock item, approach any locked door or safe.
[b]Some locked objects will have a longer interaction time, requiring the survivor’s full concentration until the door finally opens.[/b]
If you let your guard down while opening the door, surrounding enemies may strike at any moment.

[h3]● Interaction and Visual Effects:[/h3]
As you attempt to unlock a door or safe, an interaction timer will appear, showing the process of unlocking the object.
If you approach the lock with the wrong item, a message indicating the key mismatch will be displayed.
On the other hand, when you succeed, the door or safe will open, and you’ll face whatever is hidden behind it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/64eab357a7b6111785e9a479cf0ea16f5cf98ba4.png[/img]

Left image: No unlock item available for the locked door
Right image: Unlock item available for the locked door
[b]- Click or enlarge the image for a detailed view.[/b]
[b]- This image is a placeholder for understanding the system.[/b]
[h3]● Game Economy: [/h3]
Unlock items are not just one-time consumables.
They can be bought and sold via the in-game marketplace.
The rare key you find may hold immense value among other survivors.
For example, one key might be the [i][b]only key to access a location where a powerful zombie is sleeping[/b][/i], so be cautious when trading it.

[h3]● Unlock Items (Keycards and Keys): [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/2ea645c04c19fc94ed73bb48ee708b67e5fb1297.png[/img]
These aren’t just regular security cards.
Keycards serve as critical keys that grant survivors access to the hidden secrets within Liberty Grand Center.
Without a keycard, [i][b]you won’t be able to reach some of the most important places in Liberty Grand Center.[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/8706765775e4cd728a1bb3337fbc1beb81d17008.png[/img]
While the keys may seem familiar, the [b]The Midnight Walkers logo[/b] and Mogenco corporation logo engraved on them symbolize much more than just unlocking mechanisms. These keys are directly connected to [i][b]key elements of the game’s lore[/b][/i].

Soon, you’ll encounter an even greater variety of locked doors and safes, with [b]powerful enemies and unimaginable rewards hidden inside.[/b]
Where will you use your key? That decision is [b]yours[/b].

notes.title: Devlog#5
notes.notes:
In this development log, we will introduce the zombie design rework of The Midnight Walkers.

[h2][Design Concept][/h2]
The zombie characters that have been redesigned this time are based on occupations that can be frequently seen in the zombie world, and the goal is to provide a more realistic and intuitive sense of fear.
We are trying to increase the immersion in the game by turning real occupations such as firefighter zombies, police zombies, rider zombies, and high-class zombies into zombies while dealing with zombies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/362fba8a947b9e40e5fb78ce073bbbebb5944cb0.png[/img]

[h2][External Characteristics and Story][/h2]
*The zombie story is not finalized and may change during the development process.*

[h3]● Firefighter Costume Zombie[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/dc34f375d7d14defab07ecd714171471336857d7.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/a14a556fd5ef3a2878dae329859e0c6da160f086.png[/img]

[b][i]- Appearance:[/i][/b]
They wear fire suits and helmets, and have burn marks.
They move clumsily due to their heavy equipment, but are designed to look like they have high defense or health.

[b][i]- Story:[/i][/b]
They were originally under Mr. Nobody. However, they rebelled due to their dissatisfaction with Mr. Nobody, but were eventually subdued and punished by being put in charge of maintenance work for the survival show held at Liberty Grand Center.
While preparing to renovate and reopen the place after the survival show ended, they were infected by zombies that were left behind while artificially introducing zombies into the show or while putting out a fire that had spread with Molotov cocktails.
However, there is no need for sympathy. They are not honorable beings.
Their greed and betrayal caused internal divisions within the Mr. Nobody organization, and their downfall was self-inflicted.
In the zombie world, the scariest thing is not zombies. It is people.

[h3]● Front and Military Uniform Zombie[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/43aa69d943ecf8d2bd13cae9777234eb2b4ef0c3.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/b18e1fdae8872ec1ae3adfc6078b72419a6eac9d.png[/img]

[i][b]- Appearance: [/b][/i]
They have traces of wearing bulletproof vests, helmets, and military gear, and their rotten skin is characteristic.
They are designed to look difficult to deal with because of their job characteristics of military training and combat gear.

[i][b]- Story: [/b][/i]
They made a living as mercenary soldiers or riot squads during their lifetime, and acted as the main military force of Mr. Nobody. After the spread of the virus, they were hired to suppress riots and coups, and played a key role in maintaining order under Mr. Nobody's power.
However, in the process, there were personnel who suffered serious injuries from unexpected accidents or were attacked by zombies, and Mr. Nobody showed cruelty by turning them into zombies instead of killing them and using them for survival shows.
This is because survival shows always need zombies.
As they were once powerful beings who protected Liberty Grand Center, it is said that survival shows became very difficult to survive and escape after they were turned into zombies.

[h3]● Rider Costume Zombie[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/0db3a51e18817590406277e73f6818358bda78ea.png[/img]

[i][b]- Appearance:[/b][/i]
Designed to look like a fast-moving zombie wearing a bicycle helmet and light sports clothing.

[i][b]- Story:[/b][/i]
They are in charge of light material supply at Liberty Grand Center, and their primary means of transportation is bicycles.
In the world of The Midnight Walkers, electric vehicles are so valuable that they are only used when moving large quantities of materials or high-ranking officials, and general material deliveries are made by bicycle. They are responsible for quickly delivering important resources and information by bicycle.
Success brought great rewards, but failure brought a cruel fate of death or transformation into a zombie.
Before the infection, they were a vital link between survivors, playing a key role in delivering resources and information between other survivor camps and Liberty Grand Center. Success in delivering brought them great fame and rewards, but they paid a harsh price in the form of zombie transformation due to unexpected or intentional accidents.

[h3]● High-end Clothing Zombie[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/3c62452a611ab594b443157882d5e3054ba91a3f.png[/img]

[i][b]- Appearance:[/b][/i]
His once clean purple shirt, vest, and suit pants are now torn and dirty, hinting at his pre-infection social status. The glowing red eyes indicate that the infection has progressed, and the large body is designed to feel like a threatening presence capable of making slow but powerful attacks.

[i][b]- Story:[/b][/i]
This zombie is a high-ranking figure who fell victim to a power struggle at Liberty Grand Center.
In life, he played a prominent role in the community due to his resources and power, but he was pushed out of the internal power struggle and became the target of a conspiracy. His rivals deliberately infected him in order to eliminate him, and the person he trusted most was his wife.
For many years, he trusted her as his companion and political partner, but his wife secretly plotted to gain power for him. Eventually, she colluded with his enemies and forcibly threw him into the zombie horde.
He struggled to survive, but was eventually transformed into a zombie, and now he had no choice but to show the survivors his anger toward the wife he once trusted.

[h2][Planning and Development Intention][/h2]
The zombies that have been reworked this time have not yet been confirmed in terms of their detailed stats, such as their functions and health.
The zombies' stories are also the same.
Currently, we are focusing only on the external changes to provide a visually new experience.
This is to flexibly develop the zombies' abilities and characteristics by collecting various feedbacks from the upcoming playtests.

In addition, we plan to measure the psychological effect of the zombies' appearances on gameplay through A/B testing of the existing zombies and the zombies with the reworked design. Through this process, we plan to secure basic data for adjusting the game balance and scaling the difficulty.

Currently, the appearance has simply changed, but the roles and stats of each zombie may be specified based on the test results in the future. Through this, we plan to design certain zombies to play a more important tactical role in the game.

[h2][Conclusion and Future Development Plans][/h2]
We are currently improving the abilities and visual details of various zombie characters, and testing the challenges and threats each zombie will present to survivors in the game.
We will continue to update the various zombie types to further enhance the abilities and visuals of zombies through additional feedback, and to provide players with new combat strategies.
We would appreciate your participation in the upcoming playtest and various feedback.

notes.title: Devlog#4
notes.notes:
In this development log, we want to talk about the design process and role of the zombie, Screecher, in The Midnight Walkers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/073534e15728b69c766d5364147ed59638575988.jpg[/img] [b]Click the image and zoom in to see the details![/b]

[h2][Design Concept][/h2]

Screecher is designed as a female character, with distinctive features such as her face, body, and hands, all carefully crafted to leave a strong impression on survivors.

[h2][Visual Features][/h2]

[b][i]● Face and Head:[/i][/b] Screecher’s face is severely decayed, with a metal device attached to her mouth. This detail hints at a disturbing experiment she might have undergone before becoming a zombie. Ultimately, the depth of the design aims to evoke a sense of dread when survivors encounter Screecher.

[i][b]● Body:[/b][/i] Screecher's body is covered with significant wounds and deformities. Her skin bears deep scars, and some organs are exposed. All these details reflect her painful transformation process.

[i][b]● Clothing:[/b][/i] Screecher wears either a hospital gown or patient attire, hinting at her life before she became a zombie. These outfits connect her past and present, allowing survivors to speculate about her human life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/be293c3ac2dfc6b80258e9843e9e20aa8cf670aa.png[/img] [b]Screecher modeling image (without clothing applied)[/b]

[h2][Mutated Physical Features][/h2]

[b][i]● Hands:[/i][/b] Screecher’s hands have been elongated and sharpened, designed to deliver a deadly strike to survivors. The length and sharpness of her fingers further emphasize Screecher’s terrifying nature.

[b][i]● Skin Lesions:[/i][/b] Screecher’s skin is covered with grotesque, tumor-like lesions. These lesions appear almost parasitic, further amplifying the abnormal mutation caused by the zombie virus.

[h2][In-Game Abilities and Design Intentions][/h2]

[h3]- In-Game Abilities[/h3]

[b][i]● Zombie Calling:[/i][/b] If possible, avoid entering Screecher's detection range. If you spot Screecher alone, it’s recommended to take her out quickly. Screecher lets out a distinct screech, a result of extreme mutations in her throat and vocal cords, calling nearby zombies.

[b][i]● Debuff:[/i][/b] Screecher can also debuff survivors with her screech, so be careful not to get caught in its range. Her screech debuff can obscure a survivor’s vision or slow down their movement, significantly impacting their survival chances.

[h3]- Design Intentions[/h3]

[b][i]● Challenging Disruptor:[/i][/b] Screecher can be a very powerful disruptor in certain situations. Her screech can call nearby zombies, becoming a major threat to players. If not dealt with appropriately, the circumstances can quickly turn against the player. We designed Screecher to require quick and precise responses from survivors.

[b][i]● Encouraging Detours or Route Changes:[/i][/b] The presence of Screecher is intended to make survivors consider detours or alternative routes instead of facing her head-on. We wanted Screecher to stimulate strategic thinking by offering the choice to avoid or bypass the area she occupies.

[b][i]● Less Threatening Physical:[/i][/b] Screecher is a zombie that can be neutralized with proper handling. If a survivor understands her patterns and responds accordingly, she can be subdued relatively easily compared to other zombies. This design choice underscores that Screecher is a conditional threat, not a mandatory one.

Our development team doesn’t view zombies merely as in-game farming elements or monsters. In a zombie world, it’s crucial to minimize noise when dealing with zombies to avoid attracting more, or better yet, to avoid them altogether. We believe that zombies should be truly zombie-like, and humans should be able to deal with them efficiently to survive. Screecher was designed with this concept in mind, encouraging survivors to make careful, situation-based decisions.

[previewyoutube=KMObEko-Vt8;full][/previewyoutube] [b]Screecher’s screech sound is currently in development.[/b]

[h2][Development Progress][/h2]

Screecher is still in development, but we are doing our best to ensure you can face her as soon as possible. Her screech will bring new tension to Liberty Grand Center, and her grotesque appearance will deliver an unforgettable sense of dread.

We will continue to incorporate your feedback to provide diverse content in the future! Look forward to Screecher’s appearance in Liberty Grand Center :)

notes.title: Devlog#3
notes.notes:
In this devlog, we will delve into the design process of the Walker and Runner zombies that appear in The Midnight Walkers, and explore the roles they play in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/271b467d089090fe74fb498030c3e2a1ffb7018f.jpg[/img]
[b]Click on the image to enlarge![/b]

[h2][The Beginning of the Zombie Virus][/h2]

As we entered the 2020s, humanity faced the challenges of overpopulation and food shortages.
To address this, the multinational corporation 'Mogenco' launched 'The Next Lyco' project to develop a genetically modified tomato that grows quickly and is resistant to pests. This tomato became a global sensation, seen as a savior in the face of food scarcity. However, five years later, it was discovered that this tomato was the cause of a deadly zombie virus that threatened humanity.
This virus ultimately brought humanity to the brink of extinction and led to the creation of the zombies in The Midnight Walkers.
There are rumors that the zombies appearing in Liberty Grand Center are actually people who once participated in The Midnight Walkers Show, but no one knows for sure.
[b]Perhaps only those running the show know the truth.[/b]

[h2][Core Philosophy of Zombie Design][/h2]

The design of the Walker and Runner zombies goes beyond mere horror elements; they are designed to significantly impact gameplay and the strategic choices of survivors. Each zombie visually represents their background and the extent of their infection, allowing survivors to gauge their threat level just by encountering them.

[h2][Walker][/h2]

[h3]● Appearance & Design Elements:[/h3] Walker zombies are designed to move slowly. Their appearance visibly shows injuries and signs of infection on their arms and legs. These elements suggest that they were infected during an earlier stage of the outbreak.

[h3]● In-Game:[/h3] Walkers serve as minor obstacles that impede the progress of survivors. These zombies slowly approach survivors but can grab them within a certain range.
If a Walker zombie raises both hands to attack you, it’s highly recommended to dodge.

[previewyoutube=LSnfHQADL7I;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Here is a video of a Walker zombie performing a grab attack.[/b]
[b]If grabbed by a Walker, press [F] repeatedly to escape.[/b]

However, since Walkers move slowly, survivors have the option to either bypass them or take them out. Thus, Walkers require survivors to make important strategic decisions.

[h2][Runner][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44905381/8a64c633af5aaea82b735fb8fd8069547a65eaa6.jpg[/img]

[h3]● Appearance & Design Elements:[/h3] Runner zombies have a much leaner appearance compared to Walkers. The infection is more advanced, showing swollen skin and severe decay in certain areas of the body. Their slim build emphasizes that they are fast-moving zombies. Their aggressive stance immediately signals danger to survivors.

[h3]● In-Game:[/h3] Runners are aggressive disruptors that pose a significant threat to survivors. They quickly approach and attack survivors, making them difficult to shake off. In most cases, it’s challenging to ignore them, so survivors are advised to swiftly eliminate them. The presence of Runners keeps survivors on edge, requiring quick decisions and precise reactions.

[previewyoutube=jy6IFBJAbpk;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Check out the speed of the Runner zombie in this video.[/b]

[h2][Detailed Design Process][/h2]

[h3]● Face & Skin Texture:[/h3] The face of each zombie is a key element in indicating their threat level, with each being carefully designed to match the characteristics of Walkers and Runners. Walkers have relatively less decayed faces, while Runners feature severely decayed skin and exposed muscles.

[h3]● Clothing & Accessories:[/h3] Walkers are dressed in everyday clothing, reflecting the appearance of ordinary citizens with items like belt pouches and sneakers. Runners, on the other hand, are designed with a more aggressive appearance, featuring minimal clothing that exposes their decayed bodies.

[h3]● Body Deformities & Blisters:[/h3] The zombies’ bodies show various deformities depending on the level of infection, with blisters and swellings effectively conveying their deteriorated state. These visual details powerfully express the long-lasting state of living death that these zombies endure.

[h2][Conclusion][/h2]

Each zombie has its own unique role and threat level, offering survivors a diverse and intense gameplay experience. In future development stages, we plan to delve deeper into how these zombies interact within the game and how they influence survivors’ choices. Stay tuned for the next devlog!
